Title: Attempt to create an order without providing customer phone number
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and is on the order creation page
Steps:
1. Fill in the 'Customer Name' field. 2. Leave the 'Phone Number' field empty. 3. Fill in all other required fields (e.g., item type, making charge). 4. Proceed to the confirmation step. 5. Click 'Confirm Order'.

Test Data: Customer Name: John Doe, Phone Number: [empty], Item Type: Shirt, Making Charge: 500
Expected Result: The system should display an error message indicating that the 'Phone Number' field is required and prevent proceeding to the confirmation step.

Title: Attempt to create an order with an invalid phone number format
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and is on the order creation page
Steps:
1. Fill in the 'Customer Name' field. 2. Enter an invalid phone number (e.g., '123' or 'abc12345678'). 3. Fill in all other required fields (e.g., item type, making charge). 4. Proceed to the confirmation step. 5. Click 'Confirm Order'.

Test Data: Customer Name: John Doe, Phone Number: abc12345678, Item Type: Shirt, Making Charge: 500
Expected Result: The system should display an error message indicating that the phone number is invalid and prevent proceeding to the confirmation step.

Title: Attempt to create an order without selecting an item type

Steps:
1. Fill in customer details (name and phone number). 2. Skip selecting an item type. 3. Proceed to the next step. 4. Attempt to confirm the order.

Test Data: Customer Name: John Doe, Phone Number: 01712345678, Item Type: [none selected]
Expected Result: The system should display an error message indicating that an item type must be selected and prevent proceeding to the confirmation step.

Title: Attempt to create an order without being logged in (unauthorized access)

Steps:

Expected Result: The system should redirect the user to the login page or display an error message indicating that the user is not authorized to access the order creation feature.

Title: Attempt to create an order without uploading a required photo
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and is on the order creation 'Photos' step
Steps:

Title: Attempt to access the order success page with an invalid order ID

Title: Attempt to access the order success page without being logged in (unauthorized access)

Steps:

Title: Verify that malicious file uploads (e.g., executable files) are rejected during photo upload
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Click the 'Upload' button for any photo type (e.g., 'Order Cloth').
2. In the file picker, select a file with an executable extension (e.g., 'malicious.exe' or 'malicious.php').
3. Confirm the upload.
4. Observe the system response.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 with a file containing a null byte in its name (e.g., 'malicious\0.png').
6. Repeat steps 1-4 with a file containing path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../malicious.png').

Test Data: Files: malicious.exe, malicious.php, malicious\0.png, ../../malicious.png
Expected Result: The system should reject all non-image files with an error message such as 'Only image files are allowed'. The upload should not proceed, and no photo should appear in the preview or be saved to the order.

Title: Verify that oversized image uploads are rejected or handled appropriately
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Click the 'Upload' button for any photo type (e.g., 'Order Cloth').
2. In the file picker, select an image file larger than 10MB.
3. Confirm the upload.
4. Observe the system response.

Test Data: Image file: 15MB sample.jpg
Expected Result: The system should reject the oversized image with an error message such as 'Image size exceeds the maximum allowed limit of 10MB'. The upload should not proceed, and no photo should appear in the preview or be saved to the order.

Title: Verify that the photo upload API sanitizes base64-encoded image payloads to prevent injection attacks
Preconditions: User is logged in and is on the 'Add Photos' step of the order creation flow.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab).
2. Attempt to upload a valid image file and intercept the request.
3. Modify the request payload to include a malicious script in the base64-encoded image data (e.g., append ';alert(1);' to the base64 string).
4. Send the modified request.
5. If the upload succeeds, attempt to view the uploaded photo in the application.

Test Data: photo=data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mNk+A8AAQUBAScY42YAAAAASUVORK5CYII=;alert(1);
Expected Result: The system should sanitize the base64 payload and either reject the upload or strip out the malicious script. The photo should either not appear in the preview, or the script should not execute when the photo is viewed. The system should not expose any error details that reveal internal processing logic.

Title: Verify that the photo upload API enforces the API_ORIGIN restriction to prevent open proxy abuse
Preconditions: User is logged in and is on the 'Add Photos' step of the order creation flow.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab).
2. Attempt to upload a valid image file.
3. Intercept the network request to the photo upload API.
4. Modify the 'Referer' or 'Origin' header to point to an external domain (e.g., 'https://malicious-site.com').
5. Send the modified request.
6. Repeat steps 4-5 with an empty or malformed 'Referer'/'Origin' header.

Test Data: Referer=https://malicious-site.com, Origin=https://malicious-site.com
Expected Result: The system should reject all photo upload requests with a '403 Forbidden' status if the 'Referer' or 'Origin' header does not match the API_ORIGIN. The upload should not proceed, and no photo should be saved.

Title: Verify that server-side photo URLs are not exposed to unauthorized users via the image proxy
Preconditions: User A is logged in and has created an order with photos. User B is logged in with a different account.
Steps:
1. As User A, navigate to the order success page and note the photo URLs displayed.
2. Copy one of the photo URLs.
3. Log out as User A.
4. As User B, paste the copied photo URL into the browser address bar and press Enter.
5. Log out as User B and attempt to access the photo URL again.

Test Data: Photo URL from User A's order (e.g., /api/proxy/image?src=/photos/123)
Expected Result: The system should prevent User B from accessing the photo URLs directly. The browser should display an 'Access Denied' error or redirect to the login page. After logout, the system should reject the request with a '401 Unauthorized' status.

Title: Verify that session storage does not leak sensitive photo data after order completion or logout
Preconditions: User is logged in and has completed an order with photos.
Steps:
1. Complete an order with at least one photo uploaded.
2. Open the browser developer tools (Application tab).
3. Navigate to Session Storage and inspect the 'create-order:v4' key.
4. Note any sensitive data stored (e.g., photo URLs, base64 data).
5. Log out of the application.
6. Repeat step 3 and verify that the 'create-order:v4' key is cleared or contains only non-sensitive data.
7. Log in again and navigate to the order creation flow to verify that no residual data is present.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The session storage should not contain raw base64 photo data or server URLs after logout. The 'create-order:v4' key should either be cleared or contain only non-sensitive data (e.g., order metadata without photo references). After logging in again, the order creation flow should start fresh with no residual data.

Title: Verify that the photo upload API enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse
Preconditions: User is logged in and is on the 'Add Photos' step of the order creation flow.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab).
2. Rapidly attempt to upload multiple large image files (e.g., 10 files in quick succession).
3. Observe the response status and any error messages.
4. Repeat step 2 after a short delay (e.g., 1 minute).

Test Data: 10 large image files (e.g., 5MB each)
Expected Result: The system should allow the first few uploads but eventually throttle or block further requests with an error message such as 'Too many requests. Please try again later.' The system should not crash or become unresponsive.

Title: Verify that the order confirmation step does not expose sensitive data in error messages or logs
Preconditions: User is logged in and has completed the 'Add Photos' step of the order creation flow with at least one photo uploaded.
Steps:
1. Proceed to the 'Confirm Order' step.
2. Open the browser developer tools (Console and Network tabs).
3. Intercept the network request to the order submission API.
4. Modify the request payload to include invalid or malformed data (e.g., negative making charge, invalid customer phone number).
5. Send the modified request.
6. Observe the error message displayed to the user and any logs in the browser console.
7. Repeat steps 4-6 with a payload that includes sensitive data (e.g., photo URLs, customer PII) in unexpected fields.

Test Data: makingCharge=-1000, customerPhone=invalid, photoUrls={'orderCloth': 'http://internal-server/photos/123'}
Expected Result: The system should reject the invalid payload with a generic error message such as 'Invalid order data. Please try again.' No sensitive data (e.g., tokens, photo URLs, customer PII) should be exposed in the error message or browser console logs.

Title: Verify that authentication tokens are securely handled and not exposed in URLs or logs during order creation
Preconditions: User is logged in and is on the 'Customer Details' step of the order creation flow.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Console and Network tabs).
2. Proceed through each step of the order creation flow (Customer Details, Add Items, Add Photos, Confirm Order).
3. Observe all network requests and note any URLs that include tokens or sensitive data.
4. Check the browser console for any logs that expose tokens or sensitive data.
5. Log out of the application and verify that all tokens are cleared from storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies).
6. Attempt to navigate back to any order creation step using the browser's back button.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: Authentication tokens should never appear in URLs or be logged in the browser console. Tokens should be sent securely in request headers (e.g., Authorization: Bearer <token>). After logout, all tokens should be cleared from storage, and the user should be redirected to the login page when attempting to access order creation steps.

Title: Verify that order IDs are not predictable or susceptible to insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
Preconditions: User A and User B are both logged in. User A has created at least one order.
Steps:
1. As User A, navigate to the order success page and note the generated order ID.
2. Log out as User A.
3. As User B, manually construct a URL to access User A's order using the noted order ID (e.g., /orders/create/success?id=123&orderId=SHOP-YYYYMMDD-0001).
4. Attempt to access the constructed URL.
5. Repeat steps 3-4 with a slightly modified order ID (e.g., incrementing the sequence number).

Test Data: Order ID from User A's order (e.g., SHOP-YYYYMMDD-0001), modified Order ID (e.g., SHOP-YYYYMMDD-0002)
Expected Result: The system should prevent access to order details for orders not owned by the logged-in user. User B should see an 'Access Denied' error or be redirected to a safe page (e.g., dashboard). The system should not expose any sensitive order details.

Verify the order ID displayed at the top of the page. 4. Check the customer name, order date, delivery date, and trial date. 5. Confirm the total amount, paid amount (advance), and due amount are displayed correctly. 6. Verify the QR code is displayed and scannable.

Test Data: Order ID: auto-generated (e.g., '1-20240515-0001'), Customer Name: 'John Doe', Order Date: today's date, Delivery Date: tomorrow's date, Trial Date: two days from today, Total Amount: 2000, Paid Amount: 500, Due Amount: 1500
Expected Result: The success page displays the correct order ID, customer name, dates, and monetary values formatted as currency (e.g., '2,000.00'). The QR code is visible and can be scanned without errors. All details match the order submitted.

Verify the order cloth photo loads correctly without broken image icons. 6. Log out and log in using a different auth method (e.g., session cookie instead of access token). 7. Title: Verify monetary values are displayed with consistent decimal formatting
Section: Order Success Page - Monetary Value Formatting
Preconditions: User has just completed creating a new order with monetary values that may include whole numbers or decimals.
Steps:
1. Complete the order creation process and navigate to the success page. 2. Observe the total amount, paid amount, and due amount displayed. 3. Verify all monetary values show exactly two decimal places (e.g., '2000.00', '500.00').

Expected Result: All monetary values are displayed with two decimal places (e.g., '2,000.00', '500.00', '1,500.00'). No values are truncated or missing decimals.

Title: Verify that dashboard summary cards display correct counts for today's and tomorrow's deliveries
Preconditions: User is logged in and has orders scheduled for delivery today and tomorrow
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Dashboard. 2. Locate the 'Delivery Today' card. 3. Verify the count matches the number of orders due for delivery today. 4. Locate the 'Delivery Tomorrow' card. 5. Verify the count matches the number of orders due for delivery tomorrow.

Test Data: Existing orders with delivery dates set for today and tomorrow

Steps:

Test Data: Any existing customer with a photo
Expected Result: Customer photos are displayed correctly next to each customer's details. Photos load without errors and match the expected customer.

Title: Attempt to fetch an image with missing 'src' parameter
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and has access to any page that loads images via the proxy
Steps:
1. Open browser developer tools and navigate to the Network tab. 2. Trigger an image load by navigating to a page that uses the image proxy (e.g., customer list or order list). 3. Manually modify the image URL in the network request to remove the 'src' parameter. 4. Send the modified request.

Test Data: Image URL without 'src' parameter: /api/proxy/image
Expected Result: The system should return an HTTP 400 error with the message 'Missing src'. The image should not load, and an error placeholder or broken image icon should be displayed.

Title: Verify that the image proxy rejects requests with malicious 'src' parameter values to prevent SSRF attacks
Preconditions: User is logged in and has access to the application. The application is configured with a valid API_ORIGIN.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab).
2. Navigate to any page that loads customer or order photos (e.g., Customers List, Orders List).
3. Intercept the network request to the image proxy endpoint (e.g., /api/proxy/image?src=...).
4. Modify the 'src' parameter to an external URL (e.g., 'https://malicious-site.com/image.jpg').
5. Send the modified request.
6. Repeat step 4 with a local file path (e.g., '/etc/passwd').
7. Repeat step 4 with a JavaScript URI (e.g., 'javascript:alert(1)').

Test Data: src=https://malicious-site.com/image.jpg, src=/etc/passwd, src=javascript:alert(1)
Expected Result: The system should reject all requests with a '403 Forbidden' status for external URLs and local file paths. JavaScript URIs should be rejected with a '400 Invalid src' status. No image should be displayed, and the response should not contain any sensitive data.

Title: Verify that the image proxy enforces authentication and authorization for protected images
Preconditions: User is logged in with a valid access token. There exists at least one customer or order with a photo that requires authentication.
Steps: 1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab). 2. Navigate to a page that loads a protected image (e.g., customer photo). 3. Copy the image URL from the 'src' attribute of the tag. 4. Log out of the application. 5. Paste the copied image URL directly into the browser address bar and press Enter. 6. Log in as a different user who does not have access to the original user's data. 7. Repeat step 5. Test Data: Image URL from a protected customer/order photo
Expected Result: The system should reject the request with a '401 Unauthorized' status when accessed without a valid session. When accessed by a different user, the system should either return a '403 Forbidden' status or a placeholder image, but never the actual protected image.

Title: Verify that the image proxy sanitizes the 'src' parameter to prevent path traversal attacks
Preconditions: User is logged in and has access to the application.
Steps:
1. Open the browser developer tools (Network tab).
2. Navigate to any page that loads customer or order photos.
3. Intercept the network request to the image proxy endpoint.
4. Modify the 'src' parameter to include path traversal sequences (e.g., '/../../../etc/passwd').
5. Send the modified request.
6. Repeat step 4 with URL-encoded path traversal sequences (e.g., '%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd').

Test Data: src=/../../../etc/passwd, src=%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd
Expected Result: The system should reject all requests with path traversal sequences with a '400 Invalid src' status. No sensitive files should be returned, and the response should not contain any internal system details.

Test Data: Customer ID or Order ID from User A's data (e.g., 123, 456), modified ID (e.g., 124, 457)
Expected Result: The system should prevent User B from accessing customer or order details for records not owned by their account. User B should see an empty list, a 'No records found' message, or be redirected to a safe page. The system should not expose any sensitive data.

Title: Verify that the image proxy does not cache or expose sensitive images beyond their intended scope

Steps:
